```{r}
#| include: false
library(here)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(terra)
library(tidyterra)
library(cowplot)
library(png)
library(grid)
library(tidytext)
library(ggtext)
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

# Park folder and file prefix - must match 00_config.yml
park <- "abrolhos_clio-bank"
name <- "clio-bank"

# Clio Bank is a single-year (2025) survey, so the suffix on the spatial
# prediction figures is just "2025" - scripts 07 and 08 save them with
# paste(years, collapse = "-").
years     <- "2025"
yr_suffix <- paste(years, collapse = "-")

# Path helpers - keeps the chunks below free of hardcoded park/name strings
hab  <- function(f) here("plots", park, "habitat", paste0(name, "_", f))
fish <- function(f) here("plots", park, "fish",    paste0(name, "_", f))

# Draw a saved PNG at full chunk size
draw_png <- function(path) grid::grid.raster(png::readPNG(path))
```

# Natural Values

Understanding of natural values

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Sampling summary

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sampling-effort
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of monitoring campaigns in the study area, showing the survey dates, sampling method, management zones sampled, and the number of samples with each data type. SPZ = Special Purpose Zone."

# LaTeX will not break a line at an underscore, so a long campaign ID would run
# past its column. Swapping underscores for spaces lets the name wrap.
sampling_summary <- readRDS(here("data", park, "tidy",
                                 paste0(name, "_sampling-summary.RDS"))) %>%
  mutate(campaignid = gsub("_", " ", campaignid))

col_labels <- c("Date", "Campaign name", "Method", "Areas", "Samples",
                "Count", "Count", "Length")

sampling_summary %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_label(dates         = col_labels[1],
             campaignid    = col_labels[2],
             method        = col_labels[3],
             areas         = col_labels[4],
             n_samples     = col_labels[5],
             habitat_count = col_labels[6],
             fish_count    = col_labels[7],
             fish_length   = col_labels[8]) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "Habitat", columns = habitat_count) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "Fish",    columns = c(fish_count, fish_length)) %>%
  sub_zero(zero_text = "-") %>%
  cols_width(dates         ~ pct(14),
             campaignid    ~ pct(20),
             method        ~ pct(11),
             areas         ~ pct(15),
             n_samples     ~ pct(10),
             habitat_count ~ pct(10),
             fish_count    ~ pct(10),
             fish_length   ~ pct(10)) %>%
  cols_align(align = "left",
             columns = c(dates, campaignid, areas)) %>%
  cols_align(align = "center",
             columns = c(method, n_samples, habitat_count, fish_count,
                         fish_length)) %>%
  opt_row_striping() %>%
  tab_style(style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
            locations = list(cells_column_labels(),
                             cells_column_spanners(spanners = everything()))) %>%
  tab_options(table.width               = pct(100),
              table.font.size           = px(11),
              data_row.padding          = px(4),
              latex.use_longtable       = TRUE,
              column_labels.border.top.style = "none",
              table.border.top.style    = "none",
              table_body.hlines.style   = "none")
```

## Benthic ecosystem extent
### Observations

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Benthic classes observed in spatially balanced stereo-BRUV imagery, visualised as spatial pie charts. All classes scored are shown, including those too rare to model. Commonwealth marine park boundaries are shown."
draw_png(hab(paste0("scatterpie_", yr_suffix, ".png")))
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

### Dominant benthic type

```{r}

p_dom
```
